title: Nighttime lane closures scheduled on Fairfax County Parkway for bridge work Oct. 23 and 30
text:
Nighttime lane closures scheduled on Fairfax County Parkway for bridge work Oct. 23 and 30
Northbound nighttime lane closures are planned on Fairfax County Parkway in late October for bridge work tied to ongoing widening projects expected through mid-2027. Drivers should expect delays during overnight hours while crews complete improvements designed to ease congestion.
Northbound Fairfax County Parkway in Fairfax Station will experience single-lane closures and intermittent traffic stoppages on the nights of Oct. 23 and Oct. 30, according to the Virginia Department of Transportation on Oct. 21. The closures are part of ongoing bridge work associated with the Fairfax County Parkway south widening project.
The affected area is between Burke Centre Parkway and Nomes Court, specifically near the bridge over Fairfax Station Road and the Norfolk Southern Railroad tracks. Alternating left and right lane closures will take place from 10 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23, to 9 a.m. Saturday, Oct. 24, as well as from 10 p.m. Friday, Oct. 30, to 9 a.m. Saturday, Oct. 31. Intermittent traffic stoppages lasting no more than twenty minutes each are scheduled between 11:59 p.m. Friday night and 4 a.m. Saturday morning during both weekends.
Drivers are asked to be alert in these work zones due to large equipment moving in and out of the area.
The widening project aims to reduce congestion while improving safety, operations, and accessibility for bicyclists and pedestrians along approximately two miles of Fairfax County Parkway from four lanes to six between Route 123 and Nomes Court/Ladues End Lane; it also includes additional improvements such as new travel lanes on Route 123 northbound (now open), installation of concrete median barriers along tight curves, construction of a shared-use path along portions of the parkway corridor, intersection upgrades at Burke Centre Parkway including a new free-flow right-turn lane westbound, grade-separated crossings for cyclists just north of Burke Centre Parkway, enhancements at the Route 123 interchange (with some features already open), and sound wall improvements along southbound segments.
The project is scheduled for completion in mid-2027 alongside adjacent projects: The nearby Fairfax County Parkway widening north project began construction in June 2024 with similar completion goals; together they will provide six continuous through lanes across about eight miles from Route 123 to Rugby Road once finished. Meanwhile, another nearby effort—the Popes Head Road interchange—began in December 2023 with partial opening this summer after removal of an old traffic signal that had been considered a major choke point.
A temporary speed limit reduction to forty-five miles per hour remains active between Route 123 and Interstate 66 for both current projects until their completion dates arrive.
According to the official website, Virginia Department of Transportation manages one of the nation's largest state highway systems—building, maintaining and operating roads across tens of thousands of lane-miles—and provides services such as highway maintenance; it oversees planning construction efforts like this one throughout Virginia.
